title: What If Russia Nuked Ukraine? NATO's 4 Options
description:
What would NATO do if Russia used a nuclear weapon on Ukraine?

In our simulation a single 20 kiloton Iskander-M airburst over Ukrainian farmland gives NATO four options over 72 hours, and the video shows which of them cross a line.

One forty-three in the afternoon, central Ukraine: a nuclear weapon explodes over open farmland. Three minutes earlier, a launcher in Russia's Kursk region fired one Iskander-M. Nobody has three minutes to decide anything, but in the hours after the flash one question lands on every NATO table: what does the alliance do, and how long before it has to choose?

This is a simulation. It has not happened. Scenario segments are labelled SIMULATION on screen; facts are labelled REAL DATA or REAL HISTORY. The target, the launch site, the 20 kiloton yield and every NATO move are our choices, a scenario built from published analyses, not a forecast, not a known Russian or NATO plan, and we set no date. No real NATO deadline exists.

Chapters
0:00 Cold open
0:39 A missile that already exists
2:05 The answer nobody published
3:37 The strike
4:50 The first 72 hours
7:53 One warhead, ring by ring
9:08 The day after

- Atlantic Council experts on NATO responses (2022): https://www.atlanticcouncil.org/?p=521732
- NATO, the North Atlantic Treaty: https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/official_texts_17120.htm
- NATO, nuclear deterrence: https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/topics_50068.htm
- PBS NewsHour, NATO Article 4 consultations after the 2025 drone incursion: https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/nato-allies-held-article-4-consultations-after-russian-drone-incursion-heres-what-that-means

Blast, burn and flight-time figures: our scenario engine (Glasstone and Dolan, The Effects of Nuclear Weapons, 1977, calibrated to NUKEMAP by Alex Wellerstein). Target, launch site and yield are simulation choices.

How this video was made: the narration is AI-generated (Google Text-to-Speech). Scenario segments are simulations built from published models and open sources; the target, warhead, yield, NATO responses and timing are ours.
Maps: Natural Earth (public domain), OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) via OpenFreeMap and OpenMapTiles. Thumbnail backgrounds are AI-generated. Music: generated with Eleven Music.
